The '''2009–10 Bundesliga''' was the 47th season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier [[Association football|football]] league. The season commenced on 7 August 2009, with the traditional season-opening match involving the defending champions [[VfL Wolfsburg]] and [[VfB Stuttgart]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bundesliga.de/de/liga/news/2008/index.php?f=0000129862.php&fla=1|title=Spitzenspiel zum Auftakt: Wolfsburg empfängt den VfB|trans-title=Kicking off with top match: Wolfsburg hosts VfB Stuttgart|date=2 July 2009|publisher=[[Bundesliga]]|language=de|access-date=2 July 2009|archive-date=10 June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120610215754/http://www.bundesliga.de/de/liga/news/2008/index.php?f=0000129862.php&fla=1|url-status=dead}}</ref> The last games were played on 8 May 2010. There was a winter break between 21 December 2009 and 14 January 2010, though the period was reduced from six to three weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bundesliga.de/de/liga/news/2008/index.php?f=0000114325.php&fla=4|title=No mid-week matches due to shorter winter break''(Keine Englischen Wochen dank kürzerer Winterpause)''|publisher=[[Deutsche Fußball Liga|DFL]]|language=de|access-date=13 April 2009|archive-date=14 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120214170312/http://www.bundesliga.de/de/liga/news/2008/index.php?f=0000114325.php&fla=4|url-status=dead}}</ref>
The season was overshadowed by the suicide of [[Hannover 96]] captain and goalkeeper [[Robert Enke]] on 10 November 2009.

==Teams==
[[Karlsruher SC]] and [[Arminia Bielefeld]] were directly relegated at the end of the [[2008–09 Bundesliga|2008–09 season]] after finishing in the bottom two places of the table. Karlsruhe ended a two-year stint in Germany's top flight, while Arminia were relegated for the sixth time since the introduction of the [[Bundesliga]], a current record, after five years.{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}

The relegated teams were replaced by [[2008–09 2. Bundesliga]] champions [[SC Freiburg]] and runners-up [[1. FSV Mainz 05|Mainz 05]]. Freiburg returned to the Bundesliga after four years, and Mainz began a second tenure in the top division after being relegated in the [[2006–07 Bundesliga|2006–07 season]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}

A further place in the league was decided through a [[2008–09 Bundesliga#Relegation playoff|two-legged play-off]]. [[FC Energie Cottbus|Energie Cottbus]], as the 16th-placed Bundesliga team, had to face [[1. FC Nürnberg]], who finished third in 2. Bundesliga. Nürnberg won both matches by an [[Playoff format#Total points series (aggregate)|aggregated score]] of 5–0 and thus earned their seventh promotion to the Bundesliga since its introduction, also a current record. Their opponents ended a second three-year top flight tenure and left the Bundesliga without a club from former [[East Germany]] for only the second time since East German teams were included before the [[1991–92 Bundesliga|1991–92 season]], with the other time being in [[2005–06 Bundesliga|2005–06]].

===Stadia and locations===
[[BayArena]], home of [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], was expanded from 22,500 to 30,000 spectators during the first half of 2009. Other stadia which are recently undergoing renovation or expansion are [[Weserstadion]] in Bremen, [[HSH Nordbank Arena]] in Hamburg and [[MHPArena|Mercedes-Benz Arena]] in Stuttgart.

==Promotion/relegation play-offs==
16th-placed Bundesliga team [[1. FC Nürnberg]] faced third-placed [[2009–10 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] team [[FC Augsburg]] for a two-legged play-off. The winner on [[Playoff format#Total points series (aggregate)|aggregate]] score after both matches earned a spot in the [[2010–11 Bundesliga]]. Nürnberg was participating in their second playoff in a row after winning promotion at the expense of [[FC Energie Cottbus|Energie Cottbus]] in the playoff at the end of the [[2008–09 Bundesliga|2008–09 season]]. The matches took place on 13 and 16 May, with Nürnberg playing at home first.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kicker.de/relegationsspiele-terminiert-520632/artikel|title=Relegationsspiele terminiert |trans-title=Relegation play-offs scheduled|date=5 February 2010|magazine=[[Kicker (sports magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|access-date=6 February 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100207101452/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/startseite/520632/artikel_Relegationsspiele-terminiert.html| archive-date= 7 February 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> Nürnberg won 3–0 on aggregate, thus retaining their spot in the Bundesliga for the next season.
